content: Standardizing care by incorporating this recommendation into existing antenatal care packages can promote behavioral changes among healthcare providers. The implementation of these guidelines should be monitored at the health-service level as part of broader efforts to assess and enhance the quality of maternal and newborn care. For instance, methods such as interrupted time series, clinical audits, or criterion-based clinical audits can be employed to gather relevant data on pre-eclampsia and eclampsia. Clearly defined review criteria and indicators are essential, and these should align with locally agreed targets and the standards outlined in the WHO document Standards for improving quality of maternal and newborn care in health facilities. The Executive Guideline Steering Group (GSG) convenes regularly to review WHO’s current portfolio of maternal and perinatal health recommendations. This process helps WHO prioritize new and existing questions for recommendation development and updates. Consequently, this recommendation will be reviewed and prioritized by the Executive GSG. If new evidence emerges that could significantly impact the current evidence base, the recommendation may be updated. If no new reports or information are identified, the recommendation may be revalidated. After the publication and dissemination of the updated recommendation, any concerns regarding its validity should be promptly communicated to the guideline implementers, along with any plans for further updates. WHO also welcomes suggestions for additional questions to be included in the updated recommendation. Calcium supplementation during pregnancy is recommended for the prevention of pre-eclampsia and its complications. This recommendation is supported by systematic reviews and meta-analyses, which highlight the global inequities in dietary calcium intake during pregnancy. The WHO emphasizes the importance of evidence-based approaches to improve maternal and perinatal outcomes, including reducing maternal mortality and morbidity associated with hypertensive disorders.
